title: Operating Systems and Computer Networking Foundations

sources.notes: MIT OCW course identity for operating-system design and implementation: virtual memory, threads, context switches, kernels, interrupts, system calls, interprocess communication, coordination, and hardware/software interaction.

Lecture-note and reading index for OS interfaces, PC hardware, system calls, virtual memory, interrupts, locking, scheduling, sleep/wakeup, file systems, crash recovery, journaling, OS organization, scalable locks, lock-free coordination, and virtual machines; PDFs, xv6 code/book, and third-party papers remain child-resource boundaries.

MIT OCW course identity for global network infrastructure, design principles, implementation, analysis, evaluation, routing, congestion control, quality of service, mobile networking, router architectures, network-aware applications, content dissemination, security, and performance.

Lecture-note index for packet switching, internetworking, IP/TCP split, forwarding/routing, unicast routing, security, IPv6, congestion control, active queue management, fair queuing, QoS, P2P/DHTs, overlay routing, DNS, wireless/mobile networking, anonymity, multicast, scalability, and robustness; PDFs remain child-resource boundaries.
